references.text: Wisdom warns that those who reject the call will be rejected: 'Because I called and you refused, I stretched out my hand and no one cared' (Prov 1:24-25). The same principle as in the parable – those who refuse to come lose their place.

In the vineyard parable in Isaiah, the Lord asks what more he could have done for his vineyard and concludes with judgment over it (Isa 5:4-5). The parallel is God's generous invitation being rejected, followed by judgment.

The Lord says to those who abandoned him: 'I called, but you did not answer; I spoke, but you did not listen' (Isa 65:11-12). This reflects the theme in Luke 14:24 about those who refused to come to the meal.

In Matthew's parallel parable about the king's wedding feast, the invited are found unworthy because they rejected the invitation (Matt 22:2-8). The king declares that those who were invited were not worthy – corresponding to the final exclusion in Luke 14:24.

Paul and Barnabas say to the Jews: 'It was necessary that God's word be spoken to you first. But since you reject it... we turn to the Gentiles' (Acts 13:46). This reflects the pattern from the parable, where those first invited lose their place and others are invited instead.
Paul writes that Israel did not attain what they sought, but were hardened, while the chosen attained it (Rom 11:7-10). Those who rejected the call were excluded – as in the parable.

The warning about Esau, who gave up his birthright and could not get it back even though he sought it with tears (Heb 12:16-17). This illustrates the same irreversible loss that befalls those invited in the parable.

Jesus says that many will come from east and west and sit at the table in God's kingdom, while others are cast out (Luke 13:28-29). The theme is the same: those originally invited are excluded, and others take their place at the feast.

'Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb' (Rev 19:9). This eschatological meal is the final fulfillment of the image in Luke 14 – only those who accept the invitation will share in it.
